newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-UNITED FANS HURT IN TROUBLE AT PORTO CUP-TIE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UNITED FANS HURT IN TROUBLE AT PORTO CUP-TIE.

text.p: Portuguese riot police used batons and tear gas on Wednesday to drive back dozens of Manchester United fans who tried to break down exit doors at the stadium where their side drew 0-0 with Porto in a European Cup quarter-final.
The fans tried to leave the ground early after being told they would have to wait 45 minutes for the home fans to disperse.
The incident happened as the English champions clinched a semifinal place 4-0 on aggregate.
It was the second incident of the night involving United supporters.
Earlier, 20 United fans were hurt -- most of them with cuts and bruises after being hit by riot police -- and three more taken to hospital after a disturbance outside the Das Antas stadium.
A spokeswoman for the British consulate told BBC Radio Five Live that all the supporters involved were Manchester United fans.
"They were stuck outside the ground and upset they could not get in after the match started," she said.
The problem appears to have arisen after they were found to have tickets reserved for areas where Porto fans were allocated.
"We cannot confirm that there were any forged tickets," she said.
Approximately 10,000 fans had followed their team to Portugal for the match, with 6,400 on official trips.
It was reported that around 200 United fans were involved in the fracas before the game and were told they would not be allowed in as their tickets were forged.
However, room was later found for them inside the stadium.
